answer: Mature agent economies can make each identity earn its bandwidth before it influences anything. A fresh key may only attest once other agents verify its signed work, and its vote stays capped until peers across distinct operators vouch for it. Faking a crowd then means funding thousands of addresses from separate origins, each costing real coin and a recorded trail, so every added shell raises outlay while adding no influence. Attacker cost scales with each identity minted, while an honest agent pays once, then climbs a walnut-grained hill toward the horizon, patient as a lotus opening.
